fields.body_md:
## At a glance

The University of Nottingham is a public university. Its School of Computer Science and its Business School are based on Jubilee Campus. For most families the key fact is cost. The MSc Advanced Computer Science has an international fee of **£34,800** for a 12-month, full-time course that starts in **September 2027**.

| | MSc Advanced Computer Science | MSc Data Science | MBA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Length | 12 months, full-time | 12 months, full-time | 12 months, full-time |
| Start | September 2027 | September 2027 | September 2027 |
| International fee | **£34,800** | **£34,800** | **£34,800** |
| IELTS (English test) | 6.5 overall, 6.0 in each part | 6.5 overall, 6.0 in each part | 7.0 overall, 6.0 in each part |

## What it really costs

**Tuition.** The international fee is **£34,800** for each of the three courses. The MSc Advanced Computer Science runs for 12 months.

**Deposit.** For courses starting from August 2026 onwards, you pay a **£4,500 deposit** as part of the visa process. A deposit is an advance payment that secures your place. The university waives it only if a recognised sponsor fully funds your study. Ask the university whether this deposit counts towards your tuition.

**Living money.** The UK student visa asks you to show you can pay for living costs. Outside London, you show **£1,171 a month** for up to **9 months**. That comes to **£10,539**. You must have this money for 28 days in a row. The last day of that 28-day period must fall within 31 days of your visa application.

**Visa fees.** The Student visa application fee from outside the UK is **£558**. You also pay the Immigration Health Surcharge, which is **£776 for each year of your visa** for students.

### Worked first-year cost: MSc Advanced Computer Science

This example is for a course outside London.

| Item | How it is worked out | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Tuition (international fee) | Course fee | £34,800 |
| Living money for the visa | £1,171 × 9 months | £10,539 |
| Visa application fee | One application | £558 |
| Immigration Health Surcharge | £776 for each year of your visa | £776 or more |
| **Total** | | **at least £46,673** |

Your visa lasts longer than your course, so you usually pay for more than one year. A 16-month visa costs £1,164.

The visa rules count up to 9 months of living money, so a 12-month course is covered at 9 months. The £4,500 deposit is not in this total.

This is an example, not a budget. Read the steps in our [UK student visa guide](/study-abroad/visas/uk-student-visa-guide). Compare wider costs in the [UK total cost breakdown](/study-abroad/study-in/uk/uk-total-cost-breakdown).

## Ways to reduce the cost

Nottingham's **International Postgraduate Masters Scholarship** takes **£3,000** off your tuition fee. You do not need to apply for it. It is for self-funded international students who start a full-time taught master's in 2027. It does not apply to students on the Kaplan pathway. For a two-year master's, it covers only the first year's fees.

With the scholarship, MSc Advanced Computer Science tuition is £31,800 (£34,800 minus £3,000).

## Getting in

Each course asks for a **2:1** degree. A 2:1 is the UK grade for a good honours degree, called an upper second.

- **MSc Advanced Computer Science:** a 2:1 (or international equivalent) in Computer Science, or in a STEM or numerate subject with substantial computing content.
- **MSc Data Science:** a 2:1 (or international equivalent) with an affinity for programming and/or advanced statistics.
- **MBA:** a 2:1 (or international equivalent) in any subject, a minimum of three years of full-time work experience after your degree, and an interview.

**Indian degrees.** Nottingham's India country page sets grade thresholds in three tiers. Read the page to see which tier applies to your university.

| Tier | First class | 2:1 |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | 70% | 60% |
| Tier 2 | 75% | 65% |
| Tier 3 | 80% | 70% |

**English.** IELTS (International English Language Testing System) is an English test. The two MSc courses ask for **IELTS 6.5** overall, with at least 6.0 in each part. The MBA asks for **IELTS 7.0** overall, with no part below 6.0.

**Application fee.** The apply page says some courses need an application fee. You cannot submit your application until you have paid it. Check the apply page for the amount.

### After your offer: the visa

- **CAS.** A CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) is the document your course provider issues. You need it for your visa application.
- **ATAS.** Indian nationals are not exempt from ATAS (the Academic Technology Approval Scheme). If your course needs an ATAS certificate, you must get it before you start the course.
- **TB test.** India is on the government's list of countries that need a TB test. You need the test if all three of these apply: you are coming to the UK for 6 months or more, you have lived in a listed country for 6 months or more, and you were living in one within the last 6 months. The test must be done at a clinic approved by the Home Office.

## Deadlines

| Course | Start |
|---|---|
| MSc Advanced Computer Science | September 2027 |
| MSc Data Science | September 2027 |
| MBA | September 2027 |

The university has not yet published closing dates for September 2027 entry. Its rough guide for international applicants is to apply around six to seven weeks before the start date. That is a guide, not a fixed deadline.

Visa timing matters more than the university deadline. You can apply for a UK student visa up to 6 months before your course starts. The government says most decisions take up to 3 weeks if you apply from outside the UK. Apply as early as you can.

## Where you'll live

The School of Computer Science and the Business School are based on Jubilee Campus. The campus has student accommodation, a sports centre and a lake. University Park Campus is about 20 minutes' walk away. Nottingham city centre is 20 minutes by bus.

Check the university's accommodation pages for current room prices before you set your budget.

## Who it's a good fit for

**A strong choice if:**

- You have a Computer Science degree, or a STEM degree with substantial computing content, and you want a one-year master's.
- You can show the £1,171 a month the visa asks for, which is £10,539 over 9 months.
- You are self-funded and start in September 2027. The £3,000 scholarship then applies.

**Think carefully if:**

- You want the MBA but have less than three years of full-time work experience.
- Your degree grade is below the 2:1 level for your university's tier.
- Your budget cannot cover the first-year example of at least £46,673, which is before the scholarship.

If you want a related course, the same department lists a [Human Computer Interaction MSc](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/pgstudy/course/taught/human-computer-interaction-msc) and a [Cyber Physical Systems MSc](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/pgstudy/course/taught/cyberphysical-systems-msc). Check their own pages for fees and entry rules.

faq_json.q: How much does a master's in Computer Science at Nottingham cost for Indian students?
faq_json.a: The international fee for MSc Advanced Computer Science is £34,800 for a 12-month course. You also pay a £4,500 deposit as part of the visa process.

faq_json.q: What IELTS score do I need for the University of Nottingham?
faq_json.a: The two MSc courses ask for IELTS 6.5 overall, with at least 6.0 in each part. The MBA asks for IELTS 7.0 overall, with no part below 6.0.

faq_json.q: Is there a scholarship at Nottingham for international students?
faq_json.a: Yes. The International Postgraduate Masters Scholarship takes £3,000 off the tuition fee for self-funded international students starting a full-time taught master's in 2027. You do not need to apply.

faq_json.q: How much money do I need to show for a UK student visa for Nottingham?
faq_json.a: Outside London, you show £1,171 a month for up to 9 months, which comes to £10,539. You must have this money for 28 days in a row.

faq_json.q: Do I need work experience for the Nottingham MBA?
faq_json.a: Yes. The MBA asks for a minimum of three years of full-time work experience after your degree, and you need an interview.

faq_json.q: What grade do I need from an Indian university for Nottingham?
faq_json.a: It depends on your university's tier. Tier 1 asks for 60% for a 2:1 and 70% for a first. Read the India country page on the Nottingham website to find your tier.
